items.caption: Does your mind still race when you’re sitting down? Do you jump up from the sofa when someone walks in because you feel guilty for being ‘caught’ resting? 👀😩 You don’t need to earn your rest ❤️
items.transcript: I think many of us have absorbed this idea that being busy is evidence of being good. A good parent is doing, they're playing, a good partner is anticipating, a good homeowner is maintaining, a good woman particularly seems to be permanently en route to another task. Even when we sit down, part of us mentally remains standing. We are like scanning the room, we remember the appointment, we notice the finger marks on the window. The body may be on the sofa but your mind is still walking around your house with a clipboard. And because domestic work is so visible when it's not been done, it can make everything feel almost confrontational, like the washing basket sat in the corner of the room is like a witness for the prosecution. But you know what? Rest is not a reward that you claim after a sufficiently productive day. You don't have to prove that you have done enough to qualify for it.

items.caption: How to switch cleaning maintenance mode! #cleaningroutine
items.transcript: Really, really quickly, if you want to ditch the big reset to Sunday resets, you need to work out how much time you realistically have every single week. So sit down, work out where are my pockets of time. It doesn't matter if they're just 10, 15, 30 minutes a day. Work out where they realistically are. Realistically, not what you think you should have, what you actually have. And then you need to work out what are the priority top level jobs that you need to be doing in your house that are going to keep things ticking over to stop things sliding backwards, right? The idea is we're going to switch you from reactive resets to proactive maintenance cleaning. That is what we want to do. So once you've worked out the time, what you need to do, you should be having a real quick scaffold, a nice bird's eye look at what your house needs on a weekly basis, which coincidentally is how the organized method is designed to how it works. We will guide you through making sure that you are doing that in your house every week. But you've got to work with the time and the energy and the things that your house needs weekly.

items.caption:
A to-do list tells you what needs doing but a DREAD list tells you what’s quietly taking up space in your head.

These jobs are rarely particularly difficult. But every time you remember one and decide not to do it, your brain has to carry it for a little longer.

So write down everything you’ve been avoiding and pick one thing to deal with today.

Not the whole list (This isn’t a punishment). Just one small job you can finally stop thinking about.

The task might take ten minutes. The relief tends to last much longer. Get it down in the comments and then GET IT DONE ⚡️🙌
items.transcript: Come here if you have a dread list. Not a to-do list, a dread list. A list of the things that you just don't want to do and you've just been putting it off for far too long. Small jobs that you've been quietly carrying around in your brain. I want to do them, like booking the dentist, sending that email, turning the parcels. None of them are enormous, but when they all add up they can feel really, really draining. Today I've got a little bit of a challenge for you. I want you just to write it all down and I just want you to get one item off it. Kill it. Quite often the job itself can take like 10 minutes. It's the carrying it around in our brain for three weeks, three months that is the exhausting part. Once you've chosen it, tell me what it is below and we can all cheer each other on. I am going to be booking my hygiene appointment at the dentist. Not because I'm scared of the dentist, it's because I'm just not quite getting around to doing it and every single morning I wake up and go, ah, must do that. I am going to do it today.

items.caption:
Ready to get out of your constantly-looking-for-a-new-cleaning-routine era? Because I promise you, the answer probably isn’t another routine.

It’s very easy to get stuck in the cycle of finding a new system, feeling wildly motivated for three days, missing a day and then deciding the whole thing doesn’t work.

But a good routine shouldn’t require perfect conditions to keep it going. It needs to work when you’re busy. When the kids are home and when work is ridiculously hectic. 

The aim isn’t to find a routine you can follow perfectly. It’s to find one you can come back to easily. And one that is realistic enough that you’re not forever feeling behind. That’s the bit we sometimes miss.

You don’t need another fresh start. You need something boringly reliable that gives you more time to get on with your actual life.

And yes, that is pretty much why I created TOM.
Don’t pay attention to what you can do in a big house reset, instead pay attention to the normal days becuase that’s where the real data lives ❤️❤️❤️
items.transcript: It doesn't really matter what your house looks like after a two hour Sunday, Monday, Friday, whenever reset. It matters what it looks like on a regular Monday afternoon or a regular Tuesday morning. You've not done anything special. That is the real test. It's going to give you so much data, so much information. It's going to let you know whether your house is running smoothly, if it's running organised, what energy do you really have, what time do you really have without you having to have these pockets of bursts of like mad energy to do a reset. Because we can all do that and it looks great for 30 minutes afterwards, but is it sustainable?

items.caption: Staying ahead of the house is NOT about spotless rooms. It’s about doing the small things before they become big things. A made bed, dishes done, a quick wash on. Tiny jobs that stop the build-up. The mess will come back (of course it will) but you’re never quite starting from scratch ❤️🩷
❤️❤️ Finding YOUR routine
items.transcript: The only possible sanity-saving way of doing this is just to stop looking at what other people are doing. Because if you keep looking, you're always going to find more to do. And this is why it is crucial, more than ever, to work within the time and the energy and the lifestyle that you have. Anything other than that is always going to leave you feeling like you could be doing more. It's not sustainable, and it is going to burn you out. So what does that look like practically? So the first thing is to work out, realistically, how much time and energy you have on a weekly basis. Start there. It might not be a lot, but that is all that you have, right? So work with that. Then work out the stuff that needs cleaning regularly, and then divide the time and the energy that you know you have by those rooms. That's where you start. And slowly build on it if you can and if you want to.
